subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The nature of God and the Trinity
Creation, the incarnation and Jesus Christ
Salvation, sin, the crucifixion, resurrection and afterlife

questions.q: According to Christian belief, who are the three persons of the Trinity?
options: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit
The Father, the Mother and the Son
The Creator, the Prophet and the Spirit
questions.explain: The Trinity is the belief in one God existing as three persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: What does it mean to describe God as omnipotent?
questions.explain: Omnipotent means all-powerful, a key characteristic of the Christian God.

questions.q: A Christian describes God as omnibenevolent. Which statement best expresses this?
options: God knows everything past and future
questions.explain: Omnibenevolent means all-loving or all-good, so God always wills what is good for people.

questions.q: Christians believe God is just. This means God acts as a...
options: Fair judge who rewards good and punishes evil
Distant creator who ignores human actions
Being who cannot know human deeds
Force that is neither good nor bad
questions.explain: Describing God as just means God judges people fairly, rewarding good and punishing wrongdoing.

questions.q: Which statement best explains the Christian doctrine of the Trinity?
options: One God exists as three distinct persons of one substance
There are three separate gods working together
God changes form between Father, Son and Spirit at different times
God is one person with three different names
questions.explain: The Trinity teaches that God is one being in three distinct persons who share one divine substance.

questions.q: Which Christian statement of belief sets out the doctrine of the Trinity?
questions.explain: The Nicene Creed expresses belief in God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit, affirming the Trinity.

questions.q: In which book of the Bible is the Christian account of creation found?
questions.explain: The creation accounts are found in the book of Genesis, at the start of the Bible.

questions.q: John's Gospel begins, 'In the beginning was the Word.' Who do Christians understand the Word to be?
questions.explain: Christians interpret the Word (Logos) as Jesus, present with God at creation and later made flesh.

questions.q: In the Genesis creation account, what was present and active at the beginning alongside God?
options: The Spirit of God moving over the waters
questions.explain: Genesis states the Spirit of God moved over the face of the waters, showing the Spirit's role in creation.

questions.q: What does the term 'incarnation' mean in Christianity?
options: God became human in the person of Jesus
God created the universe from nothing
The soul lives on after death
questions.explain: The incarnation is the belief that God took on human flesh and became a man in Jesus Christ.

questions.q: A Christian argues that Jesus was both truly God and truly human at the same time. Which belief does this express?
questions.explain: The claim that Jesus is fully God and fully human is the core of the doctrine of the incarnation.

questions.q: Which title do Christians commonly use to express that Jesus shares the divine nature of God?
questions.explain: Christians call Jesus the Son of God to express their belief in his divine nature.

questions.q: According to Christian teaching, original sin entered the world through the actions of...
options: the people building the Tower of Babel
questions.explain: Original sin is traced to Adam and Eve's disobedience, which affected all of humanity.

questions.q: What does 'the Fall' refer to in Christianity?
options: Adam and Eve disobeying God by eating the forbidden fruit
The flood in the time of Noah
questions.explain: The Fall is the event in Genesis when Adam and Eve disobeyed God, bringing sin into the world.

questions.q: What is meant by the crucifixion?
options: The death of Jesus by being nailed to a cross
questions.explain: The crucifixion refers to Jesus being put to death by being nailed to a cross.

questions.q: On Easter Sunday Christians celebrate the discovery of the empty tomb. Which belief does this celebrate?
questions.explain: The empty tomb celebrated at Easter expresses belief in Jesus' resurrection from the dead.

questions.q: In Christian teaching, what does atonement mean?
options: Restoring the relationship between God and humanity through Jesus' death
God creating the world out of nothing
The judgement of souls after death
Living a life without any sin
questions.explain: Atonement is the belief that Jesus' death reconciles or restores the broken relationship between God and humanity.

questions.q: Christians speak of salvation by grace. What does grace mean here?
options: God's free and undeserved gift of love and forgiveness
A reward earned by keeping the law perfectly
questions.explain: Grace is the undeserved love and forgiveness freely given by God, not earned by good deeds.

questions.q: Christian belief in life after death includes judgement. This is the belief that...
options: God will judge each person on how they have lived
there is no consequence for one's actions
the soul ceases to exist at death
questions.explain: Judgement is the belief that God will assess each person's life, with heaven and hell as possible outcomes.

questions.q: A Christian struggles to accept that an all-powerful and all-loving God allows innocent people to suffer. Which issue does this raise?
options: The problem of evil and suffering
questions.explain: The tension between God being omnipotent and omnibenevolent yet allowing suffering is the problem of evil.
